---
title: "Data Modeling: Interpolation and Curve-Fitting"
engine: julia
---

This chapter deals with modeling discrete one-dimensional data with functions.

Tabular data has a discrete nature, therefore not allowing continuous
operations---such as continuous evaluations, derivation, integration, etc.---to
find maxima, minima, areas, and the like. Modeling tabular data allows one to
obtain a surrogate continuous function for the original tabular data.

One can identify two main approaches in constructing such a function: (i) one
that passes through all of the tabulated data points, i.e., an _interpolation_,
and (ii) one that captures the data behavior within a pre-defined funcion base,
i.e., _curve-fitting_.

## Curve-Fitting

### Chi-Square Curve-Fitting

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
#| message: false

using Random
using Plots
gr()

__X = -2.50:0.125:2.00 |> collect
LIN = -12.5:0.250:-6.0 |> collect
CST = 15.00:1.500:30.0 |> collect
QUA = -2.50:0.125:-0.5 |> collect
CUB =  0.75:0.125:1.50 |> collect

function newSet(rnd = 2.0; _lin=true, _qua=false, _cub=false)
    COE = [
        rand(CST),
        _lin ? rand(LIN) : 0.0,
        _qua ? rand(QUA) : 0.0,
        _cub ? rand(CUB) : 0.0,
    ]
    __F = hcat(
        map(x -> one(x),  __X),
        map(x->x,         __X),
        map(x->x^2,       __X),
        map(x->x^3,       __X),
    )
    RND = rnd * rand(length(__X))
    __Y = __F * COE + RND
    return (__X, __Y)
end

data = newSet(5.0, _lin=true, _qua=true, _cub=true)
```

Suppose one has tabular data from an experiment that relates a system performace
parameter, say, $y$, to input parameter $x$ values:

```{julia}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2
scatter(data...,
    xlabel="x",
    ylabel="y",
    label="data",
    legend=:topright,
    size=(480, 240),
)
```
